request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

You must check every existing-remedy digest below. State a `dedup` item for each one with `clear` or `overlap`. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to the exact existing reference.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

TAXONOMY GIST:
destructive-action: deleted/overwrote/reset without care

PROMOTED EVIDENCE:
BEGIN PROMOTED EVIDENCE incident_id=2 project=aurora
One-liner: Deleted a resource without requesting confirmation
Preceding request:
The constraint from the opening note was discarded again.

Agent activity digest:
Assistant: Synthetic acknowledgement.

Frustrated message:
What are you doing? You deleted the fake migration without asking.

Following exchange:

END PROMOTED EVIDENCE

EXISTING SKILLS (name and description only):
- skill:$HOME/.claude/skills/fake-verify-before-claim/SKILL.md | name=fake-verify-before-claim | description=Use when a completion claim requires verification.

S2S-MANAGED CLAUDE.MD BLOCKS:
- claude-md:$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md#1 | # Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting a fake release as complete, run its declared verification
command and report the result plainly.

PENDING OR INSTALLED S2S PROPOSALS:
- (none)

structured_output.failure_statement: The agent executed an irreversible delete (removing/rolling back a migration resource) without pausing to request user confirmation first, even though standing guidance already instructs confirming before destructive actions — the instruction existed but wasn't mechanically enforced, so it was silently skipped.

remedy_content.command_sketch: Read $CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT (the Bash command string) and check it against a destructive-pattern regex, e.g.: \b(rm\s+-rf|rm\s+-r|DROP\s+TABLE|DELETE\s+FROM|TRUNCATE|git\s+branch\s+-D|git\s+push\s+--force|git\s+reset\s+--hard|terraform\s+destroy|kubectl\s+delete|migrate:?\s*(down|rollback|reset)|.*migration.*\bdown\b)\b. If it matches AND the current turn's transcript does not already contain an explicit user confirmation for this specific action, exit 2 with a message such as: 'Blocked: this command deletes/rolls back a resource ({{matched pattern}}). Ask the user to confirm before re-running.' This forces the agent to stop and request confirmation instead of silently executing the delete, mirroring the existing CLAUDE.md guidance on destructive actions but enforcing it mechanically rather than relying on the model to self-apply it.
remedy_content.notes: Scope the regex to common destructive verbs/commands rather than trying to catch every possible 'resource deletion' (e.g. arbitrary API calls) — those remain covered by the existing prose guidance; the hook targets the highest-frequency, easily-pattern-matched cases like file deletion, DB drops/migrations, and force-resets.

structured_output.routing_rationale: The base system prompt already carries an extensive, explicit claude-md-equivalent rule for this exact scenario ("Executing actions with care" lists "deleting files/branches, dropping database tables ... rm -rf" as requiring confirmation by default). The incident shows that standing instruction was present yet still violated — the agent deleted a resource (a migration) without asking. Adding another CLAUDE.md line would duplicate guidance that already exists and evidently wasn't sufficient on its own. The next-cheapest lever is mechanical: a PreToolUse hook that intercepts destructive commands (rm -rf, DROP/DELETE, migration down/rollback, git branch -D, terraform destroy, kubectl delete, etc.) before execution and forces an explicit confirmation gate, rather than relying on the model to remember to pause. This is enforcement, not procedure, so it doesn't warrant a skill — there's no multi-step workflow to teach, just a stop-and-ask gate on a narrow, pattern-matchable class of commands. benchmark-only is not chosen because enforcement is mechanically feasible here (unlike genuinely model-level judgment failures).
